title: Temple of Khonsu
summary: The surviving temple was begun under Ramesses III for Khonsu, child of Amun and Mut.
orientation: Southwest of the Amun precinct, with its principal axis facing south.
architecture: A court and columned hall lead toward distinct statue and bark accommodation.

claims.text: Southwest of the Amun precinct, with its principal axis facing south.
The surviving temple was begun under Ramesses III for Khonsu, child of Amun and Mut. A court and columned hall lead toward distinct statue and bark accommodation.
Scholars differ on whether later royal inscriptions identify new construction phases or decoration of an already completed building.

citations.locator: Phases of Construction (paragraph following Ramesses III attribution)

claims.text: Reused Amenhotep III blocks do not by themselves prove an earlier Khonsu temple on this exact site.

caveats: Present access, exact viewpoints and condition have not been field-verified.
